That .doc's scoring key defines Locomotion = [Q1 + Q3 + Q4 + Q5 + Q8 + (7-Q13) + Q16 + Q21 + (7-Q24) + Q25 + Q28 + Q29] / 12, so the subscale in RMQ order is Q1,Q3,Q4,Q5,Q8,Q13,Q16,Q21,Q24,Q25,Q28,Q29 with reverse-worded items at within-subscale positions 6 and 9 -- exactly the positions the IRW codes mark R (locR6, locR9). The IRW code IS the S4 .sav column name (data/pierro_2018_selfforgiveness.py melts the 'loc' columns unrenamed, excluding the 'locomotion' composite), so there is no positional rename; but the .sav carries NO variable labels at all, so this is paper_order against the instrument's published order rather than data_labels. Independent content anchor from the study itself: the paper's one quoted locomotion example is 'By the time I accomplish a task, I already have the next one in mind', canonical Q21 = subscale position 8 = loc8. Item text is identical to the siblings pierro_2018_locomotion_s1 (batch_137) and _s3 (batch_138). DEVIATIONS: (a) English base fields for an Italian administration -- see translation_source; the deposit's four .sav files are label-free (S4: 51 columns, all variable labels empty, only gender carries value labels) and the article's Supporting Information holds no questionnaire, so no Italian wording is recoverable in scope. (b) translation_source=mixed: item_text and instructions are the instrument publisher's own English from the RMQ form, while the two endpoint anchors follow the study's own paper ('Strongly Disagree' / 'Strongly Agree', capitalised as the paper writes them) rather than the form's lowercase labels. (c) Anchors FLIPPED for locR6/locR9 because the stored values are already reverse-recoded -- checked here rather than inherited, since the same instrument is stored RAW in pierro_2018_locomotion_s3: alpha as stored 0.8320 / M 4.3743 / SD 0.6192 against the paper's published Study 4 .83 / 4.37 / .62, un-recoding gives 0.6669 / 4.2218 / 0.4839, and the .sav's own 'locomotion' column is the plain unrecoded mean (max |diff| 0.0, vs 0.8333 against the recoded mean). (d) option_text is endpoint-only per the paper's statement that the alternatives were 'anchored at the ends with 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 6 (Strongly Agree)'; the form's own 2-5 labels were not shipped and resp 2-5 are blank rather than padded. (e) instructions ships the form's first sentence only; its second sentence and six-point label block describe the fully-labelled canonical administration and were deliberately omitted. note: PASS WITH A REAL MAPPING CAVEAT. (1) STEP 3b -- INSTRUMENT IDENTITY, PROVEN not assumed: the four codes are the PRESENT (Shipp's 'Current') Focus subscale of the TFS and not the past or future block of the same S4 file. From the LIVE table: composite M 5.115 / SD 1.001 / alpha 0.854 against Pierro et al. Table 4's Present row 5.12 / 1.00 / .85 (L1 0.010), versus 0.160 for the Past row (5.10/1.09/.91) and 0.540 for the Future row (5.54/1.05/.92); and the live composite reproduces Table 4's whole Present correlation row -- locomotion .251 vs .25, assessment .003 vs .003, past -.094 vs -.09, future .331 vs .33 (largest deviation .004), against a Past row of -.12/.41 and a Future row of .37/.02. The live composite also equals the deposit's own 'present' column at r = 1.0000, max|diff| 0.000 over all 189 persons, so the items are stored RAW with no reverse recoding. (2) CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1, the IRW code IS the .sav column name -- data/pierro_2018_selfforgiveness.py melts [c for c in d4.columns if c.startswith('TFpresent')] unrenamed. No positional step. That does NOT grant a Step 5b exemption here, because the .sav carries no labels for the code to be authoritative about. (3) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: Study 4 ran on 189 Sapienza (Rome) students and the co-administered scales are stated to be 'the same Italian versions', so the TFS was administered in Italian; the paper does not say so for the TFS explicitly, which is an inference recorded as such. The administered Italian wording is recoverable in NEITHER the deposit (all 51 variable labels are empty; the only value labels are gender {0 Men, 1 Women}) NOR any supplement (the article's Supporting Information is exactly S1-S4 File, four .sav datasets, no questionnaire or codebook). So English sits in the base fields, language=Italian, no _translated columns, text_source=translated_substitute -- identical to the sibling pierro_2018_tf_past_s4 / tf_future_s4 (batch_139) and pierro_2018_assessment_s4 (batch_269). The 2021 Italian TFS-I postdates this study by three years, is a different translation of a REDUCED 10-item form, and was deliberately not shipped as administered text. (4) MAPPING IS UNVERIFIED AND NOT VERIFIABLE -- Step 5b NO_ROUTE. Nothing ties TFpresent1..4 to particular sentences: the .sav has no labels, the article quotes exactly one present item ('My mind is on the here and now') without a code, and all four items are same-subscale, same-range, same-polarity near-synonyms. The shipped order puts the three items whose Shipp et al. 2009 numbers are KNOWN (item 2 'I live my life in the present', item 4 'I focus on what is currently happening in my life', item 8 'My mind is on the here and now' -- recovered from PMC7851924 Table 3, whose note states 'Item number relates to Shipp et al. 2009', cross-checked against Table 9's factor pattern) at TFpresent1..3 in ascending Shipp order, and the one item whose Shipp number is NOT recoverable ('I think about where I am today'; the validation dropped items 5 and 10 without saying which was current-focus and which future-focus) last, at TFpresent4. Two cross-sample falsification attempts against the Italian validation were run and DISAGREE: the live item-total correlations (.511/.788/.753/.748) reproduce the Italian current-focus loading ranks (item 2 .672 < item 4 .704 < item 8 .751) exactly under the shipped order, while the live means (5.661/4.937/5.011/4.852) reproduce the Italian mean ranks (5.43 > 5.25 > 4.66) exactly only under the rival order that puts the dropped item at TFpresent3. Both misses are one adjacent swap; neither decides. Additionally, the premise that the .sav's numeric suffix follows the instrument's administration order at all is itself an assumption. A public_note ships. (4b) WORDING OF THE FOURTH ITEM: 'I think about where I am today' is the one shipped sentence that is NOT in the Italian validation's Table 9, because the TFS-I dropped it. It was taken from Table 1 of Olsen, Tuu & Honkanen (2023, Front Psychol 14:945487, PMC10114413, CC BY 4.0), a Norwegian study whose English column lists all four current-focus items. Three of those four are verbatim identical to Table 9's English column, which is what makes the fourth credible as Shipp's own wording; the one place Olsen differs ('My thoughts are here and now') was NOT used, because Pierro et al.'s own article quotes that item as 'My mind is on the here and now', matching Table 9. So the wording is a two-source cross-check, not a single back-translation. (5) OPTION LABELS ARE ENDPOINT-ONLY: the paper states the anchors as '(1 = Never; 7 = Constantly)', so only resp=7 carries option_text and resp 2-6 are blank rather than padded with Shipp's own 3 = sometimes / 5 = frequently, which THIS study did not report. resp=1 has no row because no respondent used scale point 1 (live resp set is 2-7; TFpresent1's own observed range is 3-7). instructions and section_prompt are blank -- no administered instruction text is published in the paper or the deposit. (6) RIGHTS: settled, not re-derived. instrument_rights_register.csv already carries a verdict=ship row for the Temporal Focus Scale (filed batch_139, silence-is-permission; no fee, permission-required, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause is locatable for Shipp/Edwards/Lambert, and the Elsevier line is a notice about the article). Applied, not rewritten; no register edit made. (7) CROSS-TABLE FINDING FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR, not a defect in this table: the two batch_139 siblings used INCONSISTENT within-subscale order conventions on the same .sav. pierro_2018_tf_past_s4 shipped ascending Shipp order (1, 6, 9, 11); pierro_2018_tf_future_s4 shipped 3, 12, 10, 7, which is neither ascending Shipp order (3, 7, 12, +dropped) nor any order derivable from PMC7851924 -- it follows a third paper's listing. Both are unverified by their own admission, so this is a consistency question rather than a demonstrated error, but it is worth an issue. (8) RETRY TEST: NO. An unchanged retry would ship exactly this file with exactly this caveat -- the block is a determinate data/source defect, not an access failure: the deposit publishes no labels and the sources publish no per-item statistics for this sample. Only a new source would change it: the authors' own Italian questionnaire form, or the Shipp et al. (2009) OBHDP appendix in its original numbering (searched and not reachable open-access -- ScienceDirect/ResearchGate/Academia only), which would at most resolve TFpresent3 vs TFpresent4 and still not pin the codes to sentences.
public_note: Item text here is the Temporal Focus Scale's original ENGLISH wording (Shipp, Edwards & Lambert 2009); the study was run on Italian students and neither the PLOS ONE article nor its SPSS deposit publishes the Italian form, so this is a same-instrument substitute rather than what respondents read. Separately, the assignment of the four sentences to the codes TFpresent1-TFpresent4 is inferred from the instrument's own item order and cannot be checked against the data: the subscale identity is solid (the composite reproduces the paper's published Present statistics, M 5.115/SD 1.001/alpha .854 against 5.12/1.00/.85, and its entire Table 4 correlation row to within .004), but the four items are same-range, same-polarity near-synonyms, so a permutation among them would be undetectable. Treat the subscale as reliable and an individual sentence's attachment to an individual code as provisional.

note: Item text = the 12 SPSS variable labels of drri1-drri12 in the PLOS S1 File, transcribed verbatim (12/12 exact string equality; drri2 lacks the canonical form's sentence-final period and was not normalised). The authors' OSF codebook lists the same 12 codes against the same 12 sentences, an independent corroboration. Code derivation is pattern 1: data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts value_vars=[f'drri{i}' for i in range(1,13)], so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- no rename, no positional step, hence Step 5b exempt and no verify_<table>.R. instructions = the study codebook's own Section G prompt, which is character-identical to the DRRI-2 Scales PDF's printed Section G instruction. option_text = the DRRI-2 form's five printed anchors (Strongly disagree / Somewhat disagree / Neither agree nor disagree / Somewhat agree / Strongly agree), used because the .sav carries NO value labels and the codebook's own rating-scale line misprints position 1 as 'Strongly Agree'; the paper's '1-Strongly Disagree, 5-Strongly Agree' corroborates the endpoints. So text_source is study_materials for item_text and instructions, canonical_instrument for option_text. The form's shared column stem 'During deployment...' and the leading ellipsis on each item were NOT shipped, because neither study source reproduces them. Direction verified on the data (N=128): the .sav's 'concern' composite equals the unreversed mean of drri1..drri12 with max |diff| = 0.000 (reversed mean off by up to 4.000) and correlates +0.403 traitanx, +0.393 ptsd, -0.179 support, so 5 = Strongly agree; raw-item alpha 0.902 reproduces the paper's .90. Step 3b: the NCPTSD page names this scale 'Perceived Threat', DRRI-2 Section G, survey label 'Deployment Concerns', and its sample item is drri5 verbatim; the form's Section G is exactly 12 items in drri1..drri12 order.
